first_reader_check.about: Whether passing a tagged released mathematics item requires the tagged competency, tested by assessment bypasses: solver policies that lack the competency by an explicit restriction on their operations or their information and pass under the published scoring rule anyway, with no student data.
first_reader_check.shown: Item-writing rules yield no family-wise discovery; one rule beats chance on two cells and awaits replication. Claimed results are measured on items re-read from the printed page, the language-model results only where a second transcription agrees. Language models of two families recover New York Regents Algebra I and Algebra II keys with the given quantities withheld, and the recovery survives a change of every option value with the form kept. On items two independent codings mark as requiring computation on the givens, one of three scorers misses the bar; those bypasses are information-restricted, so a matched pass does not require computing on the givens and whether it requires the tagged operation is left open. The international cognitive-domain cells yield no bypass at about 50 to 80 public items each.
first_reader_check.what_is_new: The assessment bypass as the object, with two restriction kinds (capability-restricted: item-writing cues, strategies, option substitution into the printed equation; information-restricted: language models denied the given quantities) that are the same object, each refuting Requirement on its cell for the part of the competency the policy was denied; the five-level claim ladder placing the paper at Requirement; hashed programs Holm-corrected inside three families; a measurement layer in which the released text is replaced by two page transcriptions; two blind item-level codings joined to the rows; an option-value control that covers every scorer.
first_reader_check.why_a_big_deal: Accountability and research read a tagged pass as evidence of the tagged competency, which assumes passing requires it. Where a policy denied the given quantities matches the key on both Regents algebra cells, on every scorer, and with the option values changed, that reading is of the wrong quantity on those items. The text layer of released forms differs from the print on about half the items, so a census that does not re-read the page measures a proxy.
abstract_says: first paragraph states the bypass phenomenon and the Requirement assumption before any channel is named: a correct answer is read as evidence of the competency, a reading that assumes passing requires it; we search for solver policies that lack the competency by an explicit restriction on operations or information and pass anyway; one-sided
measurement story in one sentence: claimed results re-read from the printed page, which the PDF text layer often misstates; language-model results confirmed by a second transcription
Algebra I and Algebra II in two model families; the recovery survives a change of every option value with the form kept (Table tab:isomorph, all three scorers, both cells)

execution statement not made: one of three scorers misses the bar on items both codings mark as requiring computation on the givens; the bypasses are information-restricted, so a matched pass does not require computing on the givens and whether it requires the tagged operation is left open (Table tab:verbclass)
EQAO not named; catalog one clause; TIMSS one unnamed clause (no bypass at about 50 to 80 public items each)
first_reader_check.no_conjunction_contradicted_by_a_table: The abstract conjoins Algebra I and II recovery with survival under the option-value change; Table tab:isomorph shows every scorer clearing on both cells under the rank-preserving arm. It does not conjoin recognition-tagged carry with isomorph survival.
first_reader_check.title_and_subtitle: Title unchanged (Does the Assessment Require the Skill?); subtitle removed at Harvey's instruction. The title is the Requirement question the paper measures a part of on each cell.
first_reader_check.intro_lead: An assessment item arrives with a claim about what answering it requires, and this paper asks whether that claim holds at the level of requirement: whether a solver that lacks the tagged competency can still pass under the published scoring rule.
